subject.title: [Performance] Duplicate parsing of CA certificates in node-extra-ca-certs.ts on every connection

question: Should this issue receive a short current-main profiling window before closure, or is the source path plus Node's startup-only contract sufficient to close it as not reproducible?
rationale: The source and dependency contract contradict the reported per-connection OpenClaw parser, but the conservative `cannot_reproduce` close requires a reasonable current-main runtime check that has not yet been performed.

options.title: Run bounded profiling
options.body: Capture filesystem and CPU stacks during parallel HTTPS requests, then close if certificate work occurs only at process startup.

options.title: Close from contract evidence
options.body: Treat the absence of an OpenClaw request-time parser and Node's startup-only loading contract as sufficient evidence that the reported path does not exist.

recommendation.title: Run bounded profiling
recommendation.body: Capture filesystem and CPU stacks during parallel HTTPS requests, then close if certificate work occurs only at process startup.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior appears to originate in their merged startup CA injection work, making them the strongest history-based routing candidate for the proof decision.
